subject: Decision Making
title: Tit for Tat
description: A 60-second lesson on Tit for Tat.

hook.text: In 1980, Robert Axelrod held a tournament: what strategy wins repeated Prisoner's Dilemma? Tit for Tat won.

buildup.text: Tit for Tat is simple. Start by cooperating. Then do whatever the opponent did last round. Mirror their behavior.

discovery.text: It is nice (starts cooperating), retaliatory (punishes betrayal), forgiving (cooperates again if they do), and clear.

twist.text: Tit for Tat never beats any opponent individually. It wins the tournament by scoring well against everyone.

climax.text: Tit for Tat shows that simplicity and reciprocity beat complex clever schemes. Start kind, punish betrayal, forgive.

punchline.text: Start kind, mirror what they do. Simplicity wins the long game.

quiz.question: Why does Tit for Tat win in repeated Prisoner's Dilemma tournaments?
options: It's simple, reciprocal, forgiving, and scores well against every type of opponent
